name: Centro (Plaza de Armas)
tagline: The rebuilt civic heart of Huaraz
description: The area around the Plaza de Armas is Huaraz's administrative and commercial core, rebuilt after the devastating 1970 earthquake into a grid of functional, mostly low-rise buildings. It holds the cathedral, banks, ATMs, the main market, and government offices, with mountain views appearing between buildings on clear days. Practical rather than picturesque.
vibe: Functional, busy, workaday Andean town center
bestFor: Errands, banking, budget lodging, market shopping
pros: Central to everything, easy walking access
Best ATM and banking access in the city
cons: Architecturally plain, little colonial charm left
Noisier with traffic and market crowds

name: Jiron Jose Olaya / Luzuriaga Strip
description: This stretch around Jiron Jose Olaya and Avenida Luzuriaga is where most foreign trekkers base themselves, packed with tour agencies, gear rental shops, hostels, and the cafes nomads actually work from, including Cafe Andino. It has the best wifi options in the city and the strongest concentration of English speakers, with a steady stream of climbers planning routes over coffee.
bestFor: Remote work in cafes, trip planning, meeting other travelers
pros: Best cafe wifi in Huaraz, including Cafe Andino
Easiest place to book treks and rent gear
Highest concentration of fellow travelers and nomads
cons: Prices run higher than the local average
Can feel touristy and crowded in peak trekking season

name: Soledad District
tagline: A quieter, more residential slice of Huaraz
description: East of the center, the Soledad district is a primarily residential neighborhood known for the Señor de la Soledad festival, one of Huaraz's biggest annual celebrations. It offers a calmer, more local pace than the tourist strip, with small neighborhood shops, family-run eateries, and easy uphill access toward mirador viewpoints over the valley and Cordillera Blanca.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a quieter, more local base
pros: Quieter and more residential than the center
Good elevated views toward the Cordillera Blanca
Cheaper long-term rentals than the tourist strip
cons: Farther from cafes and trek agencies, more walking or taxis needed
Fewer English speakers and traveler amenities

name: Carhuaz
tagline: A laid-back valley town north of Huaraz
description: About 30 minutes north of Huaraz by colectivo, Carhuaz is a small, relaxed Callejon de Huaylas valley town with its own plaza, a slower pace, and closer proximity to trailheads like Laguna 620 and routes toward the eastern Cordillera Blanca. It sees far fewer tourists than Huaraz itself, making it a genuine off-the-circuit option for nomads wanting immersion over convenience.
bestFor: Quiet immersion, trekkers seeking a less touristy base
pros: Closer to certain northern Cordillera Blanca trailheads
cons: Very limited wifi and no real cafe-work scene
Fewer services, need Huaraz for banking, gear, and larger errands
